solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Book, volume that poet edited (4,2,3,3)

indicators.note: an editor rearranges a text, so the letters of THAT POET are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: volume in the sense of space

annotation.surface: A publisher's note: this book is the volume that the poet edited.
annotation.walkthrough: The commas break the surface into a list; 'Book' stands alone as the definition while 'volume' pretends to be a second book.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: John Braine's 1957 novel about an ambitious young man in a Yorkshire town carries this title.

entries.clue: Cheese starts to ripen in August, firm and dry inside (7)

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are their first letters
something inside is held within, so firm and dry sit within those first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Ripen, In, August

annotation.surface: A cheesemaker's tip: let it ripen in August, firm outside and dry within.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dry' as TT (teetotal) is a standard crossword abbreviation, and the cheese-ripening surface makes it sound like texture.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a soft Italian whey cheese.

entries.clue: Speech helping to support head of organisation (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the upper, so the helping sits under the O
the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A talk that helps prop up whoever runs the organisation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Helping' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun: a portion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a formal address delivered on an occasion.

entries.clue: Taking lid off, burps as Aga cooks veg (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue the lid is the top letter, so burps loses its B
cooking changes the ingredients, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: Lift the pan lid and the vegetables bubble noisily as the Aga cooks them.
annotation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy British range cooker. 'Taking lid off' looks like kitchen action, but it beheads BURPS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the green spears are a vegetable.

entries.clue: Put cover on sofa, maybe (5)

blocks.note: the athletics sense, as in putting the shot
a light blanket draped over furniture

annotation.surface: An instruction to drape a cover over the sofa.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'put' as 'place'; the first definition is the shot-putter's sense, to hurl.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the shot-put hurl, and the loose blanket laid over a sofa.

entries.clue: Prohibition boosted interest in hardcore rock genre (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upside down, so GRAB reads BARG
'in' puts one thing within another, so the raised word goes within the genre

blocks.note: the genre grew out of 'emotional hardcore' punk
to interest someone: how does that grab you?

annotation.surface: Banning a music style only made fans keener on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Interest' reads as a noun in the surface, but it works as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an official ban, especially on trade.

entries.clue: In match, perform better than away game (7)

annotation.surface: In a match, a team performs better than usual in an away game.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is long and runs naturally into the wordplay; 'than' marks where it ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: beating opponents by playing more skilfully.

entries.clue: Goal heralding defeat for boss of mine (12)

indicators.note: a herald arrives first to announce what follows, so the goal goes before the defeat

annotation.surface: A goal signalling that the gaffer's team has lost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boss of mine' reads as 'my boss'; the mine is a pit, and the hunter's goal doubles as the workplace.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the person in charge of an open-pit mine.

entries.clue: Release clutch when parking behind relative briefly (7)

indicators.note: a car parked behind another comes after it, so P goes last
cut short, so UNCLE loses its last letter

blocks.note: P = parking, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A driving lesson: let the clutch out when parking behind a relative's car.
annotation.walkthrough: The motoring surface makes 'clutch' a pedal; in the definition it is a grip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to open a grip and let go.

entries.clue: Automatic rifle shell warning (7)

indicators.note: to shell is to strip the outer casing, so NOTICE loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: to rifle a drawer is to steal from it
warning = NOTICE, minus its outer letters

annotation.surface: A notice about a semi-automatic weapon and its ammunition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Automatic rifle' and 'shell' fuse into a gun story; 'shell' is actually a verb telling you to peel the warning.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mechanical, done without thought, like a machine.

entries.clue: Leaflet saying “Spades and Cutting Tools” (8,4)

annotation.surface: A flyer advertising a garden-tools shop.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'Spades and Cutting Tools' look like a shop name, hiding that the last two words are the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: power tools with a spinning toothed disc.

entries.clue: More and more cross grass bank (7)

definitions.note: 'More and more cross' means crosser, the comparative

blocks.note: to grass on someone is to inform on them

annotation.surface: Someone getting ever angrier with a grassy bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer, and to grass is to inform. 'Ratty' is British for irritable.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal sense: ratty means irritable, and this is its comparative.

entries.clue: Bird biting round bilberry now and then (7)

indicators.note: turning something round reverses it
only some of the letters show up, every other one

annotation.surface: A bird pecking round a bilberry bush every so often.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Biting' is an adjective here, as in a biting wind, not the bird's beak at work.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a family of small songbirds.

entries.clue: Heed the terms of Forestry Commission fences for pine (5)

indicators.note: a term is an end, so take the last letters
a fence encloses a field, so the two letters enclose the heed

blocks.note: last letters of ForestrY and CommissioN
to give ear is to heed

annotation.surface: Mind the rules: the Forestry Commission puts fences round its pine plantations.
annotation.walkthrough: The Forestry Commission is the UK body that manages state forests. 'Pine' looks like a tree but is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to long for something absent.

entries.clue: Congrats from university, after old academic year beset by some stickiness (4,2,3)

indicators.note: the university letter comes after the rest
to be beset is to be surrounded, so the stickiness wraps around the old academic year

annotation.surface: A university congratulates you on finishing a messy old academic year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Academic year' reads as one phrase but splits: the academic and the year are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom of praise, much like 'well done'.

entries.clue: Completed tie ending in Everton showing a loss (9)

indicators.note: the end of Everton is its last letter

annotation.surface: A football cup tie is played out, and Everton end up beaten.
annotation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club. The football surface points at a lost match; the definition is about a bank account.
annotation.definitionFit: A banking sense: an account in debit, owing money.

entries.clue: Handle on post? (9)

blocks.note: the surface wants a grip; the setter means slang for a name
the surface wants a gatepost; the setter means written on mail, so: whose name is on the envelope?

annotation.surface: Something to grip fixed on top of a gatepost.
annotation.walkthrough: A handle is slang for a name, and post is mail, so the clue asks for the person named on a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: the name on a piece of mail belongs to the person it is sent to.

entries.clue: Small scene, one revolving around Jupiter in Cymbeline? (7)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing within another, so the moon sits within the play

blocks.note: Cymbeline is a Shakespeare play, an example of a play

annotation.surface: A tiny stage scene with an actor circling Jupiter in a production of Cymbeline.
annotation.walkthrough: Jupiter really appears in Cymbeline, descending on an eagle, which makes the surface plausible; here he is the planet. The question mark flags Cymbeline as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a small three-dimensional model of a scene.

entries.clue: Finally, foal neighs, wiggling tongue (7)

indicators.note: take only the final letter of foal
the letters squirm into a new order

annotation.surface: A young horse whinnies, its tongue waggling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' pictures the foal's mouth, but it means a language.
annotation.definitionFit: Tongue in the sense of a language; this one is spoken in Britain and far beyond.

entries.clue: Port and some curaçao negligently knocked back (5)

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used
a drink knocked back goes down the hatch; here the letters go backwards

annotation.surface: Someone carelessly downing a glass of port and some curaçao.
annotation.walkthrough: The drinks surface makes 'Port' a wine; it is a seaport. Curaçao is an orange liqueur.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a major Italian seaport on the Ligurian coast.

entries.clue: Juice in US leads to spasm around base of tender stomach (7)

definitions.note: 'stomach' is used as a modifier, as in stomach ache; the answer is the adjective

indicators.note: the fuel comes first and leads on to the rest
'around' means surrounding, so the spasm wraps round the letter from tender
in a down clue the base is the bottom, the last letter

blocks.note: juice is slang for fuel; Americans call petrol gas

annotation.surface: American fruit juice brings on cramps in a sensitive stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'juice' a drink; it is fuel. The phrase 'gastric juice' hides in the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: The medical adjective for things of the stomach, as 'stomach' works in 'stomach upset'.

entries.clue: Held in New York, American thug angrily defiant (7)

indicators.note: someone held in a city is detained within it, so the middle pieces sit within NY
an angry thug is shaken up, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: An American hoodlum detained in New York, raging and refusing to cooperate.
annotation.walkthrough: The gangster scene makes 'defiant' sound grown-up; the answer is a nursery word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually of children: disobedient, badly behaved.

entries.clue: Study husband cutting gristly meat at last (7)

indicators.note: a knife cutting meat goes into it, so the husband goes into the gristly meat
take the last letter of meat

annotation.surface: A husband studies a chewy cut of meat on his plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Meat' seems to belong with gristly; only its last letter is used, and the toughness comes from 'gristly' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Study in the sense of reflection, as in 'lost in a brown study'.

entries.clue: Wild animal concerning ass when upset (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the letters upside down

annotation.surface: A wild beast that is annoyed by a donkey.
annotation.walkthrough: Git is British slang for a stupid or unpleasant person.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the big striped cat of Asia.

entries.clue: Remains in court with son and quarrels (4-3)

blocks.note: what is left of a body
to be up before a court is to be on trial

annotation.surface: Someone is still in court with their son, fighting over something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb, stays; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: rows or scuffles.

entries.clue: Dig near fragments in settlement on the Thames (7)

indicators.note: to fragment is to break into pieces, which can be reassembled in a new order

annotation.surface: Archaeologists excavate close to pottery fragments at a riverside site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fragments' reads as a noun in the archaeology picture; it is the verb that breaks up DIG NEAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a large town on the River Thames, west of London.

entries.clue: Hurricane possibly seen here in two broadcasts (7)

blocks.note: the first broadcast: to put on the airwaves

annotation.surface: A storm that might be spotted in a couple of weather bulletins.
annotation.walkthrough: The Hawker Hurricane is a Second World War fighter plane; the weather-forecast surface wants a storm.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: vintage aircraft such as the Hurricane are flown at such displays.

entries.clue: “Meet and greet” in Glasgow that precedes the big fight? (9-3)

blocks.note: in Scots, to greet is to weep

annotation.surface: Pre-match hype in Glasgow: the handshakes before a big boxing bout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Meet and greet' looks like one phrase, but it splits into two words. Glasgow signals Scots usage.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the summons that calls fighters to assemble before battle.
